costDetail.src: PA Report 1/2026 (Machap & Melaka Pinda), sections 5, 6, 7, 9 (Tables 5, 6, 22, 24; Appendix 1)
notes: All cost figures are for the whole estate (Machap+Melaka Pinda combined): PA RM amounts over combined FFB 22,258.13 t (budget 24,321 t) and RM/ha over the combined 1,014.82 ha. The PA report gives no Machap-only costs or FFB.

Group totals and total are as printed in PA Table 24. The four printed group figures add to RM302.90/t (the figure quoted in PA item 17 and 11.17), not the RM302.95/t printed as the Table 24 total and in 9.1.

Upkeep & cultivation: Table 24 actual RM92.48/t equals Table 6 spending EXCLUDING upkeep supervision (RM2,058,516.89 / 22,258.13 t); including it gives RM94.77/t. The budget RM100.57/t INCLUDES upkeep supervision (RM2,445,867 / 24,321 t; RM97.72 without). Items shown include upkeep supervision, so they add to 94.76, not the printed 92.48. Table 24's own RM/t CPO column agrees: upkeep RM490.48/t CPO x 4,300.62 t CPO / 22,258.13 t FFB = RM94.77/t FFB, and total RM1,579.56/t CPO = RM305.20/t FFB, so the CPO column includes upkeep supervision but the RM/t FFB column does not.

Harvest & collection items are per tonne as printed in PA Table 22 (sub-total 97.27 vs Table 24 97.26; budget 92.09 vs 92.08). External transport RM33.85/t (budget 31.80) is shown separately, as Table 24 does, under Despatching & selling; Table 22 total incl. transport RM131.12/t vs RM123.89.

Upkeep and general-charge items are calc: RM amounts in PA Table 6 and Appendix 1 divided by actual FFB 22,258.13 t and budget FFB 24,321 t (Table 23). General charges have 38 lines in Appendix 1; the 13 largest by actual are shown and the other 25 summed. They reproduce Table 24 GC 79.31/72.61 within rounding.
Table 6 items add to RM2,109,349.71 vs printed RM2,109,349.89; Appendix 1 'other expenses' items add to RM468,627.67 vs printed sub-total RM468,627.17.

summary: FY2025/26 (May 2025–Apr 2026, Machap+Melaka Pinda combined): 22,258.13 t FFB, 21.93 t/ha vs 23.96 budget (-8%) and 27.79 a year earlier (-21%) (PA, Agro).
Cost RM302.95/t vs RM297.06 budget (+2%, combined); harvesting & collection incl. transport RM131.12/t, driven by MTG breakdowns (infield loading RM23.14 vs 15.58) (PA).
Machap division: 19 of 21 sub-blocks yielded less than FY2024/25; MC2008 fell 35–52% while young MC2022A/B rose 42–52% (Agro Table 16).
Ganoderma is the main threat: last census about 11% dead and 10–12% infected palms; mounding done on 137 ha; compost trial shows spears opening (Agro, PA).
Machap fields: pruning 3 of 3 rounds done, selective spraying 88%, circle spraying 51% (held back where mounding keeps circles clean); 95 workers vs 101 needed (combined) (PA).

issues.title: Cost of production RM302.95 or RM302.90/t; upkeep basis differs
issues.detail: PA Table 24 and 9.1 print RM302.95/t, but its four lines (79.31 + 92.48 + 97.26 + 33.85) add to RM302.90, which item 17 and 11.17 quote. Table 24 upkeep actual RM92.48/t excludes upkeep supervision (RM2,058,516.89 / 22,258.13 t; with it RM94.77/t, total about RM305.19/t), while the budget RM100.57/t includes it (RM2,445,867 / 24,321 t). Actual vs budget for upkeep is not like for like. Table 24's RM/t CPO column (upkeep 490.48, total 1,579.56) converts at 4,300.62 t CPO / 22,258.13 t FFB to RM94.77 and RM305.20/t FFB, i.e. it includes supervision while the RM/t FFB column does not.

issues.title: FY24/25 yield basis: 27.79 t/ha looks to use about 919 ha
issues.detail: Agro Table 16 block yields x Agro/PA block hectares give about 25,535 t for FY24/25, matching PA last-year FFB 25,533.21 t, but that is 25.16 t/ha on 1,014.82 ha, not the 27.79 t/ha printed (25,533.21 / 27.79 = 919 ha). For FY25/26 the block yields add to about 21,046 t (20.74 t/ha) vs PA 22,258.13 t (21.93 t/ha). The reported 21% fall (PA, Agro 7.2/7.5) partly reflects a change of area basis.

issues.title: PA says pruning complete; its table shows 82%
issues.detail: PA item 14 and 6.9.2 say all fields completed 3 rounds; Table 18 shows 749.09 + 749.09 + 983.40 = 2,481.58 of 3,040.32 ha programmed, with MP1994A/B, MP1995A, MP2002B, MP2005A/B/C pruned only in round 3 and MP2003A not at all. Agro 5.2.3 confirms only one round in MP1994, MP2002, MP2005. Machap (MC) fields did all 3 rounds. Table 18 also lists MP1994A as 36.97 ha (38.35 elsewhere) and totals 1,013.44 ha. PA Table 18 shows MP2002A pruned in all 3 rounds; Agro Table 11 shows MP2002A in round 3 only.

issues.title: Ganoderma census date and level disagree
issues.detail: PA 6.3.3.2: latest census May 2025, 11.08% dead and 10.29% infected 'compared with 129,970 healthy palms' (that is the total stand, 129,968 in Agro). Agro 3.2: April 2025 census, 11% dead and 12% infected. Agro item 2 and 7.9: last census 2024, estate yet to do a new one.

issues.title: MC2008 block yields inconsistent with bunch data
issues.detail: Agro Table 16 FY25/26: MC2008A 11 bunches x 16.81 kg x 137 SPH = about 25.3 t/ha but printed 16.70; MC2008B 11 x 16.49 x 140 = about 25.4 vs 18.55; MC2008C 12 x 18.25 x 134 = about 29.3 vs 14.45 (-52%). All other sub-blocks agree within about 5%. Either the yields or the bunch counts for MC2008 are wrong.

issues.title: MC2022 palm stand: three different figures
issues.detail: Agro Table 1 flags census 20,241 palms (A 8,106, B 7,359, C 4,776) vs sub-block summary 21,264 (8,349, 7,970, 4,945); this 1,023-palm gap is the 129,968 vs 130,991 estate total in Agro 2.5. Appendix 2b fertiliser programme uses a third set: 8,334 / 7,841 / 4,908 (SPH 151 / 136 / 149). PA Tables 13 and 14 also swap MC2022A and MC2022B hectares (57.45 and 55.12).

issues.title: Labour recruitment overspend misquoted
issues.detail: PA 5.2(d) gives the overspend as 'RM40,69.50 (29%)' and says recruitment and renewal costs totalled 'RM57,400.00 against a RM24,800.00 budget'. Appendix 1: RM180,946.50 vs RM140,250 budget, +RM40,696.50 (129% of budget, i.e. 29% over). The items listed in 5.2(d) add to RM123,546.50, matching neither figure.

issues.title: Pest & disease cost per ha misquoted
issues.detail: PA 6.3.3.3 gives RM77.79/ha vs budget RM179.98/ha; Table 6 shows RM77.73 vs RM176.98.

issues.title: Yield typo and period labels
issues.detail: PA 11.16 says '2,193 tons per hectare' (21.93). Both reports' summary pages are headed 'Visit for 2/2025' (PA) / '2-2025' (Agro) though they are 1/2026. PA Appendix 1 page 2 is headed 'YEAR 2024/2025' while page 1 is 2025/2026. PA Table 14 barn owl columns are headed MAY'24 / APRIL'25 though text refers to April 2026.

issues.title: Barn owl boxes: 44 (PA) vs 62 (Agro)
issues.detail: PA 6.3.1.2 and Table 14: 44 boxes, 1 per 23 ha, 7 occupied (16%). Agro 5.5.10: the estate has 62 barn owl boxes.

issues.title: Replanting year for MP2003A labelled two ways
issues.detail: PA 2.5, 11.1 and Agro 3.28: MP2003A (30.04 ha) replanting in FY2026/27, felling began July 2026. Agro Appendix 2c says 'cease manuring prior to replanting (FY2027/28)'; Agro 4.2 calls the halted NK block '(4.93 ha)' though 4.93 is tonnes of NK Mix.

issues.title: Supply palm table total is meaningless
issues.detail: Agro Table 5 totals the cumulative 'to date' column as 4,925 palms; the latest cumulative figures are 854 (2022A) + 485 (2022B) + 219 (2022C) = 1,558. The 'today' total of 483 is correct.

issues.title: NK Mix applied 149.37 (PA) vs 149.42 mt (Agro)
issues.detail: PA Table 11 NK Mix rows give 55.11 + 55.11 + 39.15 = 149.37 mt (total applied 1,180.86 mt); Agro Table 9 says 149.42 mt (total 1,180.91). Mix A is used in the FY2026/27 programme but its nutrient specification is not listed in Agro Appendix 2.

issues.title: Harvesting machine coverage and counts differ
issues.detail: PA 7.4: 3 EV Badang used in the young palm area 'covering 265.56 hectares'; PA Table 20: EV Badang covers 145.41 ha (MC2022) and 265.56 ha is MTG 3 & 4's area. Table 20 areas add to 1,015.59 ha vs 1,014.82 planted. PA 7.1 says 4 MTG (7.3: 3 working + 1 backup) while Table 20 lists MTG 1 to 5 and Table 25 five mini tractors.

issues.title: Circle spraying rounds and interval range
issues.detail: PA Table 7 MC2002A: 51.10 of 153.30 ha completed (33%, one round) but 'completed rounds' 0. PA item 15, 7.12 and 11.13 give harvesting intervals of 11 to 19 days; Table 21 shows 10–13 days in MC2020A and MC2022A.

issues.title: MP1991A shown as merged and as still separate
issues.detail: Agro Table 16 lists MP1991A (FY24/25 21.20 t/ha) as 'Combined with P94A', and no area table includes it (PA Table 2, Agro Tables 2-4 total 1,014.82 ha), yet Agro 2.3 lists MP1991A (2.15 ha) among small sub-blocks that still remain.

actions.item: Raise harvester output above 1.5–2.2 t/man-day (PA target over 3.0): 1 harvester per 22 ha tall / 25 ha young, 12–16 per MTG, 5–6 per Badang
Keep harvesting intervals under 15 days; tall-palm areas still over 15 days while harvesters helped at Leong Hin San
Improve harvesting intervals in tall palm areas to cut crop losses
Align the work programme with the schedule to avoid backlogs
Reassess farm and mini tractors; write off or sell badly damaged units (running costs 27–213% over budget)
Consider outsourcing mechanised infield collection, manuring and grass cutting
Weeding contractor to take on the whole process (workers, chemicals, transport) in the long run
Carry out a new Ganoderma census using the advised method (last census 2024)
Dig mounding soil properly for upcoming mounding work
Replant MP2003A (Melaka Pinda) under the Ganoderma SOP from Agro 1-2025 and 2-2025; consider a watermelon intercrop
Keep full stand (148 SPH) in MC2020 and MC2022 for the first 5 years; record total palms and SPH on gross planted area
Add palm censuses: with the Ganoderma census before replanting, and yearly in young or flood-prone fields
Reconcile palm stand records (MC2022: 20,241 vs 21,264; estate 129,968 vs 130,991)
Merge remaining small sub-blocks (MC2002E, MP1991A, MP2002A/B) into 30–50 ha units
Fix wet floor in fertiliser store, now worse (study Batu Anam's peripheral drain)
Close the gap between the fertiliser schedule and application; manure young mature, then prime, then old palms; don't carry FY2026/27 balance beyond Apr 2027
Try semi-mechanised manuring (EV Crawler/Badang, 35 bags/day) instead of manual broadcasting
Finish road grading before the monsoon (by September); none done in FY2025/26 despite 1,000 chains budgeted
Patch roads (consider crusher run); grade MC2022C; fix waterlogging on graded road in MC2002E
Do rat census every 3 months and bait when damage exceeds 10% (second-generation bait)
Bait rat-affected sub-blocks as one group in one direction (not adopted in the last campaign)
Improve barn owl occupancy (16%): find the cause; try Bright Farm or USM design boxes, place at least 6 palms from roads, clean yearly
Install T-perches (wooden crossbar) in MC2022 until palms are tall enough for owl boxes
Stay alert for bagworm; plant beneficial plants estate-wide (60% Cassia cobanensis, 20% Antigonon, 20% Turnera)
Run bunch and rat censuses as a programme; thin palms systematically with records
Eradicate Tetracera, Lantana, wild brinjal and VOPs
Spot-spray weed patches in vacant interrows for a complete kill before they seed
Fit one-sided nozzle covers or baffles on mistblowers to protect Axonopus ground cover
Establish soft grass ground cover on bare ground in MC16A and MC02A
Stop over-pruning still seen in MC22A/B/C and roadside MP19A; fix one-sided pruning and frond stacking in MC22C; keep 2 fronds below the lowest bunch
Stack cut fronds at a slant between 4 palms to ease machine movement
Retrain harvesters and evacuators: no bunches left in drains, less trash in loose-fruit bags
Resolve cattle intrusion through discussion or the legal channel
Merge small sub-blocks MC2014A+B and MC2014C+MC2016A
Remove abnormal/unproductive (runt) palms in MC2016 and MC2020
Complete palm mounding (17,829 palms, 137 ha); none needed next year
Complete FY2025/26 manuring without further NK/Mix B delays (99% applied)
Replace broken and unsuitable soft pallets in the fertiliser store (phased)
Catch up circle weeding in MC22, MC20A and MP19A; control Mikania in MC22B
Implement progressive pruning in all fields (PA says done; PA Table 18 shows Melaka Pinda fields short of 3 rounds)
Follow up rat baiting in MC2020 and MC2022 and keep treatment records

kb:
MACHAP ESTATE, United Malacca Berhad (UMB group). IMPORTANT: both reports cover "Machap & Melaka Pinda Estate" as one estate with two divisions, Machap (MC fields, 722.58 ha) and Melaka Pinda (MP fields, 292.24 ha). This dashboard is for Machap. Crop, yield, cost, labour, manuring and general-charge figures in the PA report are only given for the whole estate and are labelled (Machap+Melaka Pinda combined). Block figures (area, SPH, yield, weeding, pruning, fertiliser) are Machap-only where the report gives them per field. Sources: PA Report 1/2026 (Planting Advisor En. Adnan Bin Mustafa, visit 9 July 2026, previous visit 16 December 2025, review period May 2025 to April 2026, 12 months = FY2025/26) and Agronomy Report 1/2026 (Senior Agronomist Mr Lai Hong Heng, visit 29 June 2026, previous visit 22 December 2025, manuring programme FY2026/27). Estate Manager Mr Livindran A/L Ganesan (Estate Manager I, Grade 12, joined estate May 2021; also oversees Leong Hin San Estate). Plantation Controller (Peninsular Malaysia) Mr Low Fook Sin. Financial year runs May to April.

AREA (PA Tables 1-2, Agro Tables 2-4, April 2026). Whole estate (combined): title 1,121.88 ha; oil palm 1,014.82 ha, all mature (90.46% of title); other crops 5.78 ha (stevia and pepper 3.10, durian 1.18, Founder Garden 1.50); pineapple on TNB rentis 13.31 ha; unplanted 87.97 ha (roads 70.36, swamp/pond 0.30, unplantable 12.39, quarry 1.68, buildings 3.24). Machap division 722.58 ha: MC2002 160.34 ha (A 51.10, B 29.78, C 46.13, D 25.05, E 8.28), MC2005 162.35 (B 34.18, C 55.66, D 37.41, E 35.10), MC2008 117.21 (A 31.63, B 47.30, C 38.28), MC2011A 25.42, MC2014 33.55 (A 11.85, B 13.70, C 8.00), MC2016A 44.29, MC2020A 34.01, MC2022 145.41 (A 55.12, B 57.45, C 32.84). Melaka Pinda 292.24 ha: MP1994 81.78, MP1995 55.23, MP2002 28.37, MP2003A 30.04, MP2005 85.74, MP2019A 11.08. Machap SPH (Agro Table 4, census 2024): MC2002 105 (A 100, B 97, C 114, D 104, E 119), MC2005 132 (B 149, C 128, D 129, E 126), MC2008 137, MC2011 122, MC2014 139, MC2016 155, MC2020 136, MC2022 139 by census. Estate average 128 SPH, 129,968 palms. Agro: sub-blocks merged as advised: MC2014A+B into MC14A (25.55 ha), MC2014C+MC2016A into MC16A (52.29 ha); small blocks MC2002E, MP1991A, MP2002A, MP2002B should be merged into 30-50 ha units. Age profile (whole estate): 18.8% young mature, 21.7% prime, 46.0% mature, 14.0% old. Many toppled palms and vacant points in mature areas (MC02A, MC02E, MC08A, MC05E). Target 148 SPH for MC2020 and MC2022 during first five years; supply palms planted in MC2022 (to Feb 2026: 2022A 854, 2022B 485, 2022C 219 cumulative) replacing abnormal clonal palms with seed-derived material. Census every two years; extra census before replanting and yearly in young or flood-prone fields. Replanting: MP2003A (Melaka Pinda, 30.04 ha, 82 SPH, severely Ganoderma-infected) felling, chipping and de-boling began July 2026 for FY2026/27.

STAFF (PA Table 3): Estate Manager, 2 Assistant Managers (Muhammad Arieff Bin Abdul Rahman: harvesting and pineapple; Hazrah Binti Zainul Abidin: other cash crops), 2 harvesting field conductors, 1 upkeep field conductor, 2 general clerks; 3 field supervisors; adequate, no change.

LABOUR (PA Table 4, combined): April 2026 95 workers vs 101 required (-6), down from 97; June 2026 93. Ratio 1 worker to 11 ha (on 1,033.91 ha incl. cash crops). Cutters 33 vs 27, carriers 23 vs 26, MTG drivers 5 vs 4, FFB mandore 2 vs 3, tractor drivers 3 vs 4, LF collectors 2 vs 4, sprayers 4 vs 5, manuring 5 vs 4, circle raking 0 vs 2, security 3, lorry drivers 2, pineapple/stevia/pepper 6 vs 7. Harvesters incl. mechanised collection drivers and collectors 61 (cutters+carriers+MTG drivers 61 vs 57 required in the table), ratio 1 to 17 ha, judged adequate. Contractor harvesting MP1994A, MP1994B, MP1995A and MP2005C (194.06 ha) quit over contract rates. PA 7.1: 56 checkroll harvesters with 4 MTG and 3 EV Badang.

GENERAL CHARGES (PA Table 5 and Appendix 1, combined, May 2025-Apr 2026): RM1,765,238.76 vs budget RM1,765,954; RM1,739.46/ha vs 1,740.16, on budget. Management and supervision RM560,732.40 (RM552.54/ha vs 626.81); labour and amenities RM735,879.19 (RM725.13 vs 656.98, 110%); office and related RM451,269.29 (RM444.68 vs 437.04); office and premises upkeep RM17,357.88. Over budget by more than 10%: labour wages and allowance +RM8,365.80 (12%, contract completion incentive RM49,400 and price bonus RM27,015.80); labour EPF +RM27,053 (77%, unbudgeted foreign worker contributions); labour welfare +RM11,032.42 (75%, retirement benefit, new workers, festivals); labour recruitment RM180,946.50 vs RM140,250 (+RM40,696.50, 29% over; levy RM83,542.88, medical RM21,662; PA text misprints the overspend as RM40,69.50); cess/rate/rent RM119,993 vs RM75,221 (+RM44,772, 60%, quit rent provision).

UPKEEP AND CULTIVATION (PA Table 6, combined, 12 months): RM2,109,349.89 vs RM2,445,867; RM2,078.55/ha vs 2,410.15. Per ha actual vs budget: upkeep supervision 50.09 vs 68.17; weeding 223.85 vs 268.26 (17% under, rounds deliberately delayed where mounding keeps circles clean); manuring 1,241.80 vs 1,502.53; pest and disease 77.73 vs 176.98; census and thinning 6.63 vs 18.39; drains 23.07 vs 21.33; roads and bridges 138.37 vs 179.37; soil and water conservation 122.47 vs nil (unbudgeted mounding); boundaries 20.42 vs 16.05 (fencing MC2022 against cattle); supplying 17.19 vs nil; pruning 155.28 vs 156.76; tools 1.65 vs 2.32.

WEEDING (PA Tables 7-10; Agro Table 13). Circle spraying whole estate 1,848.81 of 3,480.69 ha programme, 1.82 rounds, 53% (MC2022 programmed 6 rounds, others 3). Machap fields only: 1,321.23 of 2,603.97 ha, 51%. MC2016A no circle spraying (bare ground from close planting); MC2002C/E and MC2022B circles due at visit. Contract RM35/ha; worker RM11/ha, 6.20 ha/day; MC2022 RM18/ha, 3.65 ha/day. Selective spraying whole estate 2,514.42 of 3,044.46 ha, 2.48 rounds, 83%; Machap fields 1,903.70 of 2,167.74 ha, 88% (2 of 3 rounds in MC2002D, MC2008B/C, MC2014C, MC2022A/B/C). Mistblower, triclopyr round 1, metsulfuron rounds 2-3; RM14/ha, 6.0 ha/day; MC2022 RM15/ha, 4.4 ha. VOP spot spraying 115.48 ha (MC2002E, MC2011A, MP1994A/B) with KRUSH. Remove Tetracera, Lantana, wild brinjal; Asystasia and Clidemia in 2019 and 2022 fields. Agro: ground cover well managed, Axonopus compressus dominant; weed control improved, no over-spraying; bare ground in MC16A and MC02A; fit one-sided nozzle covers on mistblowers. MC22B Mikania much reduced (Agro).

MANURING (combined). PA Table 11 FY2025/26: 1,180.86 of 1,185.78 mt applied; Mix B 775.92, Comp 25 48.58, NK Mix 154.30 (39.15 of 44.08 in Feb), kieserite 29.23, RP 177.76. 4.93 mt NK Mix for MP2003A halted for replanting; PA calls the programme complete. Agro Table 9: 1,180.91 of 1,185.79 mt, 99%. Mechanical spreader on flat land, manual broadcasting on hills, terraces, young palms: 17-24 bags per man-day at RM14/ha, RM65.38-70.00/day; semi-mechanised (EV Crawler/Badang, 35 bags/day) suggested. Agro: fertiliser store floor wet and worse, even in empty bays; study Batu Anam peripheral drain. Prioritise young mature, then prime, then old palms. FY2026/27 programme (Agro Appendix 2, no amendments, kg per palm): MC2002 Mix A 2.00 x4 (May, Jul, Oct, Feb) = 8.00; MC2005 Mix A 2.00 x4 (Jun, Sep, Nov, Feb) + RP 1.00 Jan = 9.00; MC2008 Mix B 2.20 May then 2.00 Aug, Nov, Mar + RP 1.00 = 9.20; MC11A and MC14A Mix B 2.00, kieserite 1.00 Jul, Mix B 1.70 Aug, 2.00 Nov and Mar, RP 1.50 = 10.20; MC16A Mix B 2.00 x4 + kieserite 1.00 + RP 1.50 = 10.50; MC20A Mix B 1.70 x3, RP 2.00, Mix B 2.00 = 9.10; MC22A/B/C Mix B 1.50, 1.70 x3, RP 2.00 = 8.60. New planting: 600 g CRF 20:6:14:3 + 500 g RP per hole.

LEAF ANALYSIS (Agro 5.3 and Appendix 3, samples Aug 2025): N and K mostly normal, P and Mg normal to moderately low. Machap samples N 2.49-2.87%, P 0.156-0.167%, K 0.96-1.20%, Mg 0.20-0.30%. Palms show good vigour, no widespread deficiency.

PESTS AND DISEASES. Rat (PA Table 13): baiting 704.31 ha with STORM 1 piece per palm, 1-4 rounds (MC2014, MC2016A, MC2020A, MC2022, MP2019A). Agro Table 14 rat damage: MC2016A 8% Sep, 16% Jan; MC2020A 10% Jul, 15% Jan, 9% Apr; MC2022A 11% Aug, 11% Feb; MC2022B 10%, 12%; MC2022C 11% Jun, 21% Feb; MC2014A/B/C 14%, 18%, 16% Jan; MP2019A 19%. Post-baiting (Table 15): 3-8% except MC2022B 10% and MC2022C 16%; T-perches advised in MC2022. Barn owls: PA 44 boxes, 7 occupied (16%), try Bright Farm boxes (90% occupancy at Far East Holdings); Agro says 62 boxes, annual cleaning, USM design. No bagworm outbreak. Pest and disease cost RM77.73/ha vs 176.98. Ganoderma: PA census May 2025 11.08% dead, 10.29% infected. Agro: April 2025 census 11% dead, 12% infected; elsewhere says last census 2024 and a new one is still due; mortality rises about 2.5% a year after age five. Agro dissected 8 palms in MP03A: all had over 60% of the base bowl damaged, even normal-looking palms; infection starts at the base; mounding grows new roots but is only temporary. Compost trial MP05B (30 March 2026, 10 palms, 30 kg QL chicken-manure compost each): unopened spears fell (e.g. M3 3 to 0, M5 2 to 0 by July), 1 palm toppled. Rainfall Apr-Jul 2026: 191.7, 340.4, 141.4, 201.7 mm (Feb 243.0, Mar 27.0).

SOIL CONSERVATION (PA Table 15): mounding on 17,829 palms, 137 ha (MC2005C 6,498, D 4,013, E 3,443; MC2014A 1,545, B 1,213, C 1,117) at RM7.20/palm = RM128,368.80; complete, unbudgeted (RM122.47/ha). Agro: proper excavation still not done.

ROADS, DRAINS, BOUNDARIES (PA): no lateriting; grading 0 of 1,000 chains budgeted, started July 2026, finish by September; backhoe 900 h road repair and 115 h culverts at RM52.50/h; RM138.37/ha vs 179.37. Drains: backhoe 423 h; RM23.07/ha. Boundary drains adequate; cattle intrusion unresolved.

PRUNING (PA Table 18, Agro Table 11): Machap fields all 3 rounds done (Jun, Oct, Dec 2025). Melaka Pinda fields mostly only round 3, MP2003A none; PA nevertheless says all complete. Cost RM155.28/ha vs 156.76. Agro: Machap pruning satisfactory; slightly more dry fronds in MC02B, MC08C, MC05C; over-pruning in MC22A/B/C and roadside MP19A; one-sided pruning and fronds in circles in MC22C; keep two fronds below lowest bunch for palms under 15 years; pruning paid 3 times a year, 4 from next year.

HARVESTING (combined). MTG system in tall palms (MTG 1-2 on 466.84 ha 26.02 t/day; MTG 3-4 on 265.56 ha 25.81 t/day; MTG 5 on 137.78 ha 21.24 t/day), 3 EV Badang in MC2022 145.41 ha at 7.76 t/day (capacity 15). Harvester output (PA Table 19, Machap): MC2002 2.00 t/man-day at RM37/t (RM74/day); MC2005 2.10 (RM73.50); MC2008 2.20 (RM72.60); MC2011 2.10; MC2014 1.60 at RM32 (RM51.20, lowest); MC2016 2.20; MC2020 1.50 at RM45; MC2022 1.20 at RM65 (RM78). Melaka Pinda 1.50-2.00 t at RM35-53. PA calls 1.5-2.2 t low. Intervals April 2026 (PA Table 21): Machap 10-19 days, Melaka Pinda 18-19 days; rounds to date 21-32. Agro: 24.9 rounds in FY2025/26 (2.1/month; young and prime 2.2, tall 1.8 vs targets 2.5-3.0 and 2.0-2.5); intervals over 20 days in Aug-Oct 2025 as tall-palm harvesters were sent to Leong Hin San and new recruits still training. Quality MC2008B 5% overripe; trash in loose-fruit bags; bunches left in drains (MC05E); crop losses minimal; crop recovery 104% FY25/26 vs 89% FY24/25. Harvesting and collection cost (PA Table 22, combined): RM2,918,476 = RM131.12/t vs RM123.89 (+6%); before external transport RM97.27/t vs 92.09; infield loading RM23.14 vs 15.58 (+49%, MTG breakdowns); harvesting own FFB 43.49 vs 39.45; contract 9.99 vs 16.71; external transport 33.85 vs 31.80.

CROP (PA Table 23, combined, May 2025-Apr 2026): FFB 22,258.13 t vs budget 24,321 t (-8%); last year 25,533.21 t. Yield 21.93 t/ha vs 23.96 budget and 27.79 last year. CPO 4,300.62 t, OER 19.32% vs 18.02% budget (19.76% last year); kernel 1,114.60 t, KER 5.01%; CPO 4.24 t/ha. Agro yield history (combined): FY2021/22 19.95, FY2022/23 27.80, FY2023/24 27.45, FY2024/25 27.79, FY2025/26 21.93 t/ha (-21.1%); bunches per palm 14 to 12, bunch weight 13.79 to 13.88 kg. Machap sub-block yields FY25/26 vs FY24/25 (Agro Table 16, t/ha): MC2002A 19.96 (23.48), B 13.05 (17.17), C 21.07 (25.82), D 19.42 (25.16), E 22.73 (28.97); MC2005B 25.46 (32.61), C 25.87 (31.42), D 23.87 (26.91), E 28.04 (30.64); MC2008A 16.70 (25.54), B 18.55 (30.01), C 14.45 (30.35); MC2011A 20.93 (26.66); MC2014A 28.65 (34.59), B 28.94 (33.59), C 26.04 (37.77); MC2016A 26.96 (37.09); MC2020A 22.40 (23.99); MC2022A 17.00 (11.96), B 11.56 (7.61), C 10.60 (12.48). Machap-only estate yield is NOT given in either report. Calculated from Table 16 block yields x block hectares it is about 20.2 t/ha for FY25/26 (FY24/25 about 24.8); treat as indicative only. Do not divide the combined FFB 22,258.13 t by Machap's 722.58 ha: the FFB is for both divisions (1,014.82 ha). Block table prevYtd = FY2024/25 (May 2024-Apr 2025). Melaka Pinda FY25/26: MP1994A 25.08, MP1994B 24.90, MP1995A 23.26, MP2002A 19.94, MP2002B 14.57, MP2003A 12.86, MP2005A 22.20, B 24.57, C 21.08, MP2019A 26.50. Only MP2019, MC2020 (smaller fall) and MC2022 held or improved.

PRODUCTION COST (PA Table 24, combined, 12 months): RM302.95/t FFB vs RM297.06 (+2%; item 17 and 11.17 say RM302.90): general charges 79.31 vs 72.61; upkeep 92.48 vs 100.57; harvesting and collection 97.26 vs 92.08; despatching and selling 33.85 vs 31.80. Per t CPO RM1,579.56 vs 1,648.16. Reasons: crop shortfall, high vehicle costs; upkeep low as manuring stopped in replant block and circle spraying held back.

VEHICLES (PA Table 25, combined): management vehicles and lorry within budget. 5 Landini farm tractors RM17.62-34.65/h, four 27-68% over budget (WD 3708F RM17.62 vs 22.45, under); 5 mini tractors (MTG) RM13.95-29.43/h vs RM7.67-14.18, 82-213% over, due to breakdowns; reassess, write off or sell badly damaged units.

HARVEST MACHINES: PA 7.4 says the 3 EV Badang cover 265.56 ha of young palms but Table 20 puts them on MC2022 145.41 ha. DATA CAVEATS: see the issues list.

ffbProd.notes: Both tonnages are for the whole Machap & Melaka Pinda Estate (1,014.82 ha: Machap 722.58 + Melaka Pinda 292.24); neither report prints a Machap-only tonnage, so the whole series is combined. Melaka Pinda has no page of its own, so there is no double count. No FY2026/27 (May 2026 onward) tonnage printed, so no ytd. Agro 7.2 and its yield chart give t/ha only for FY2021/22–FY2023/24 (19.95, 27.80, 27.45); no tonnes for those years. FY2024/25 25,533.21 t at the printed 27.79 t/ha implies about 919 ha, not 1,014.82 (see issues). PA Table 23 last-year CPO differs slightly between columns (5,046.56 same period vs 5,046.58 12 months). PA 11.16 misprints the FY2025/26 yield as 2,193 t/ha.
